title: Algebraic realization of finite curvature jets
statement: For a fixed dimension and order \(k\), characterize the pointwise arrays \((R,\nabla R,\ldots,\nabla^kR)\) realized by a Riemannian metric with prescribed zeroth-order inner product. The notebook asks for the algebraic relations among these tensors.
status: As of 9 November 2026, settled in the finite-order realization formulation by the classical metric-jet isomorphism theorem. The exact modern algebraic-jet conditions and sufficiency are read in Jentsch, Definition 1 and Theorem 3; this checked 2026 revision is not the date of the theorem's discovery. Pre-1965 normal-tensor and curvature-reduction theory is documented through the Thomas/Veblen/Schouten tradition, with the earliest complete modern identity list not independently dated here. No minimal invariant-ring-presentation problem is inferred. \citep{jentsch2026jet,janyska2011reduction,thomas1926identities}

title: Intersections of the zero torus with its Hamiltonian image
statement: For the zero section \(T^n\subset T^*T^n\), bound the number of intersections with its image under a compactly supported Hamiltonian diffeomorphism. The transverse formulation asks for at least \(2^n\) intersections; in the possibly degenerate formulation the cup-length lower bound is \(n+1\). The notebook writes only exact periods and an unqualified \(2^n\), so these additional hypotheses are explicitly reconstructed.
status: As of 9 November 2026, both stated Hamiltonian bounds are established. The unqualified \(2^n\) version is false: a graph of the differential of \(\sin x+\sin y-\sin(x+y)\) on \(T^2\) has three intersections. No open general Arnold-conjecture variant is inferred from this record. \citep{chaperon1983questions,auroux2026floer,gong2023cuplength}

title: Multiplication of distributions conormal to transverse submanifolds
statement: For transverse smooth submanifolds \(S,T\subset X\), determine a sufficient class of distributions singular on them whose product is canonically defined, including \(P\delta_S\) and \(Q\delta_T\) for properly supported classical pseudodifferential operators. Mere information about singular supports is not a sufficient formulation.
status: As of 9 November 2026, settled for the stated conormal class by the wavefront multiplication criterion. H\"ormander's original Theorem 2.5.10, pp. 126--127, is read; pseudodifferential operators do not enlarge wavefront sets, and transverse conormal bundles have no opposite nonzero covectors. Bott's flat-trace theorem is the contemporary graph/diagonal case. The later terminology is a reconstruction, not a quotation from the notes. \citep{bott1966report,hormander1971fourier}

title: The folds and cusps of z squared plus epsilon conjugate z
statement: Determine the real singularities and critical-value curve of \(F_\varepsilon(z)=z^2+\varepsilon\overline z\), \(\varepsilon\ne0\).
status: As of 9 November 2026, solved: the critical locus is \(|z|=|\varepsilon|/2\), with three ordinary cusp points and folds at all other critical points; its image is a three-cusped hypocycloid. The same example is published in Arnold's 1968 exposition, Example 6. The determinant, caustic and ordinary-cusp tests are independently checked here. \citep{arnold1968singularities}
